_comment: Declares the ELEVEN document categories a VIP-based verification
environment is built out of, and which real extractor in this repo
converts each one. Data, not scattered hardcoded logic -- same
policy-as-data shape as dv_harness/context_budget.policy.json and
dv_harness/harness_deploy.manifest.json. Extend THIS file for a
project's own document categories, never doc_extraction_fanout.py.
`extractor` names the real module.callable that HANDLES the category.
How to invoke it lives in doc_extraction_fanout.CATEGORY_EXTRACTORS,
because the eleven extractors have eleven genuinely different
signatures and a JSON-encoded call convention would be a second,
wrong-by-construction description of code that already exists. The two
are held together by assert_extractor_table_matches_categories(), so a
category added here without an adapter -- or an adapter naming a
callable that no longer resolves -- fails a test rather than silently
dropping a category out of the fan-out.
`extractor: null` is a REAL, DELIBERATE answer, not a placeholder. Two
of item #40's categories genuinely have no extractor in this codebase,
and each says why in `no_extractor_reason`. Reporting NO_EXTRACTOR is
the honest result for those; inventing a stub that produced an empty
artifact would make an absent capability look present.

categories.title: VIP document / user guide
categories.notes: Real pypdf text extraction for .pdf; .txt/.md read directly. Output is consumed by env_manifest.build_user_guide_refs().

categories.title: VIP source code / reference class library
categories.notes: Declarations and file:line locations ONLY -- never method bodies, which is what makes indexing a context-budget tier-1 tree legitimate at all (assert_no_bodies_retained()).

categories.title: VIP examples (env / config / interface / scoreboard / sequence / seq_item / test / constraint / coverage / callback)
categories.no_extractor_reason: No distiller exists in this repo. context_budget.policy.json leaves VIP `Examples/` directly READABLE as a deliberate tier-1 carve-out (denying the sanctioned reference material is the false positive that gets a gate switched off). A read permission is not extraction into a structured artifact, and no code turns an Examples/ tree into one.

categories.title: DUT document / register description (doc, excel)
categories.notes: An input-CONTRACT transcription/validation pipeline, not an autonomous .doc/.xlsx parser: design_intent.py's own docstring says it transcribes and validates, never authors. The .doc/.xlsx -> structured-source step is performed by a human or an agent reading the document.

categories.title: IP document / user guide
categories.notes: Same input-contract caveat as 40d. Every legal-drop/backpressure condition REQUIRES a document+section citation, so an uncited (i.e. possibly invented) condition cannot validate.

categories.title: Programming guide (register write order / wait conditions)
categories.notes: Same input-contract caveat as 40d. Supplies the Gate-2 mode-bit precondition connectivity.py never had.

categories.title: DUT RTL / source / interrupts / registers
categories.notes: Real `verible --export_json` RTL parsing via verible_parser.py. Every layer reports its own honest status, so a missing verible binary yields NOT_AVAILABLE with a reason rather than an empty port list. Interrupts specifically remain agent-skill-driven (interrupt-event-dispatch), not a coded extractor.

categories.title: IP source code / behavioural model
categories.no_extractor_reason: No module in this repo is named or scoped for IP source distinct from VIP source. vip_symbol_index.py indexes a VIP class library (svt_*-shaped reference classes); pointing it at an arbitrary IP RTL/model tree would produce a symbol index labelled as a VIP reference, which is a wrong artifact rather than a partial one.

categories.title: Top testbench / running script / filelist
categories.notes: Covers the running-script/filelist half. The top-testbench HIERARCHY half (hierarchy.json) has a declared producer -- the CORE/hierarchy-discovery skill -- but no non-agent extractor, per CLAUDE.md's Context Budget section. That half is therefore NOT produced here and is not claimed to be.

categories.title: Reference command.txt / BFM pattern files
categories.notes: Mechanical register-write macro extraction plus host/DUT paired-block symmetry analysis. Escalation into the question queue is deliberately NOT performed from the fan-out -- see doc_extraction_fanout.py's 'reading is never a mutating act' note.

categories.title: Standard protocol specs (AMBA / USB / PCIe / MIPI-CSI2 / MIPI-DSI / eMMC / SD-SDIO / CAN-FD / Ethernet)
categories.notes: Deliberately the SAME mechanism as 40a, not a second one: vip_user_guide_distill.py's own CLI help says 'OFFLINE distillation of a VIP user guide (or any protocol spec document)'. Only doc_kind differs (protocol_spec vs vip_user_guide), so a later reader is never left guessing which kind of document a reference points at.
